newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Norscan Oct pulp stocks up 20,000 tonnes - source.
newsitem.headline: Norscan Oct pulp stocks up 20,000 tonnes - source.

text.p: North American and Scandinavian (Norscan) pulp stocks rose by 20,000 tonnes in October, preliminary figures from consultancy group Momentum showed on Friday.
"Total inventories for NorScan are likely to have risen by a marginal 20,000 tonnes," the consultancy group Momentum said in a statement.
It said the figures were only preliminary and that some Swedish figures were excluded and there was uncertainty about some of the Canadian figures.
"Swedish figures are missing but information available is indicating production/shipments in the 85-percent range and unchanged or a small decrease in inventories.

"However there is at the same time some uncertainties about whether stocks of Canadian pulp in Atlantic European ports are sold or unsold and included or not in the Canadian statistics on inventories," Momentum said.
No total figure was given. In September Norscan stocks totalled 1.73 million tonnes.
The average for the last eight years' October figures is an increase of 40,000 tonnes compared with the previous month.
Last week rumours hit the market of an increase of up to 250,000 tonnes. Later a Finnish forestry company said its forecast was unchanged while another said its was for a rise of 100,000 tonnes.
Sodra Cell's marketing director said on Thursday he believed the NorScan stocks had risen by 23,000 tonnes, except Swedish stocks which he believed to be at largely unchanged.
